subject: Request: Geo-model isolation for MedSys pilot — no automatic failover
messages:
From: Alex Jensen <alex.jensen@medsys.io>
To: hannah_schmitt@redwood.com
Date: 2026-08-25T09:12:00-04:00
Subject: Pilot gating: must keep all EU traffic pinned to eu-large-v2 (no fallback)

Hi Hannah —

Thanks again for the demo yesterday. Quick ask from our side as we move to the pilot: MedSys cannot permit automatic failover to US regions or to quantized/compat model variants for this pilot. Our legal & data residency team require that inference for EU patients remain in EU data centers and run on the eu-large-v2 model family for the duration of the trial.

Specifically:
- No automatic region failover to non-EU hosts;
- No fallback to quantized or smaller model variants that materially change output (we need eu-large-v2 only);
- A documented exception process and SLA commitments if capacity constraints prevent serving on eu-large-v2.

Can Redwood support a strict routing lock and a formal exception flow (we understand there may be cost/availability implications)? We’re targeting a soft launch on 2026-09-20.

Appreciate a quick confirmation so we can align procurement/legal.

—Alex
Alex Jensen
Head of ML Platform, MedSys Health
From: hannah_schmitt@redwood.com
To: karthik_iyer@redwood.com, stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Cc: alex.jensen@medsys.io
Date: 2026-08-25T10:03:00-04:00
Subject: Fwd: Pilot gating: must keep all EU traffic pinned to eu-large-v2 (no fallback)

Team — forwarding a customer ask that’s coming up fast. MedSys wants a strict geo + model lock for their pilot and an exception flow if capacity becomes constrained. They understand there will be cost/availability tradeoffs but need a formalized agreement.

Please advise:
1) Can we technically pin requests from their account to EU-only and disallow cross-region failover?
2) Can we refuse automatic fallback to quantized variants for a specific customer and surface a clear error path/backoff?
3) What SLAs/commitments do we need to offer to mitigate their legal concerns?

I’ll coordinate a short call with MedSys if needed, but we need an internal decision to scope procurement and legal asks.

Thanks — Hannah
Hannah Schmitt
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
From: karthik_iyer@redwood.com
To: hannah_schmitt@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Cc: stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com
Date: 2026-08-25T15:22:00-04:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Pilot gating: must keep all EU traffic pinned to eu-large-v2 (no fallback)

Hannah / team —

Short answers up front: technically feasible, but operationally risky without reserved capacity. Details:

- Region lock: we can enforce routing policies per-customer so that requests are only routed to EU clusters. That’s straightforward in the control plane.

- No-fallback guarantee: we can implement a customer-level policy that prevents automated fallback to other model families or regions. However, if the eu-large-v2 pool is saturated (or a node fails), requests will queue or error rather than failover.

- Availability options: to meet their needs we should propose reserved capacity (Dedicated) for the pilot window and an SLA addendum that defines availability targets and acceptable error modes. Without dedicated capacity, we can only promise best-effort with clear documented behavior on how the router will behave under full load.

Action items for scoping:
- Product: produce an ops runbook for the exact router behavior (error codes, retry windows, queue limits).
- Sales: propose a Dedicated capacity add-on pricing for the pilot dates.
- Security/Product: confirm any audit/logging requirements for residency proof.

I’ll draft the minimal config change and a list of required infra/ops steps if you want me to own the tech side.

—Karthik
Principal Product Manager, Routing & Runtime
From: stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com
To: hannah_schmitt@redwood.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com, alex.jensen@medsys.io
Date: 2026-08-26T09:08:00-04:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Pilot gating: must keep all EU traffic pinned to eu-large-v2 (no fallback)

Hannah / Karthik —

Security & compliance notes: we can support the residency requirement, but need to collect the following from MedSys before we sign off on a no-fallback SLA:

1) Data classification & retention policy for the pilot (health data = high sensitivity).
2) Regulator contact / country-specific constraints (any local EU jurisdiction requirements?).
3) A signed statement that MedSys accepts the operational failure mode (errors/queueing) in the event of capacity issues, unless they purchase reserved capacity.

Also recommend a brief risk summary for their legal team outlining the residual risks of strict geo/model-locking (I’ve attached a template). If they insist on no fallback and no dedicated capacity, we should escalate for executive approval — that’s a business risk we should price accordingly.

—Stephanie
Head of Security & Compliance, Redwood Inference
From: hannah_schmitt@redwood.com
To: Alex Jensen <alex.jensen@medsys.io>, ml-platform@medsys.io
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.com, stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: 2026-08-27T14:05:00-04:00
Subject: Re: Pilot gating: must keep all EU traffic pinned to eu-large-v2 (no fallback)

Alex —

Thanks — we can support a strict EU-only, eu-large-v2 model lock for the pilot, but it requires a short list of commitments from both sides:

1) Redwood asks MedSys to procure dedicated capacity for the pilot window (recommended) so we can guarantee availability and avoid queueing behavior. We will provide pricing options and capacity numbers once product/infra finalizes the runbook.

2) If MedSys chooses not to purchase Dedicated capacity, Redwood will enforce the routing lock but will define an error mode (429/503 responses and no automated failover). We will include the exact error semantics in the ops runbook.

3) Security requires the documents Stephanie requested (data classification, retention, jurisdiction notes). Please see the attached SLA exception form and risk summary for the legal team to review.

Next steps:
- Hannah to schedule a 30-min call with MedSys + Product (Karthik) tomorrow to walk the pilot config and timeline.
- Karthik to share a draft router ops runbook by EOD 2026-08-27.
- Stephanie to share the risk template and required security evidence.

Alex — can you confirm whether MedSys prefers Dedicated capacity or wants to try with hosted (best-effort) first? If Dedicated, procurement will need targeted capacity numbers; Karthik will provide those on the call.

Regards,
Hannah Schmitt
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Attachments:
- redwood-sla-exception-form-v1.pdf (SLA exception template; fill & sign)
- medsys-risk-summary.xlsx (security: please complete and return)
